Repr.addAppParen adds parentheses iff the surrounding precedence is at least maxPrec (1024). But as I understand, in Lean function application has leadPrec (1022). This gives:

import Lean
open Std.Format Lean.Parser

/-- info: "some 0" -/
#guard_msgs in
#eval pretty <| reprPrec (some 0) argPrec

I.e., with argPrec (1023), function application is formatted without parentheses. But in Lean, a function application in argument position must have parentheses.

The following formats correct only because reprArg also uses a "wrong" precedence (maxPrec instead of argPrec):

/-- info: "some (some 0)" -/
#guard_msgs in
#eval pretty <| reprPrec (some (some 0)) 0

So why do Repr.addAppParen and reprArg use maxPrec instead of leadPrec and argPrec, as Lean does?

The reason I am asking, is that I spend quite some time being confused by this. If for some reason maxPrec indeed is correct in this case, it should be documented why that differs from the actual Lean precedences.
